name: pk_to_sk_retrieval_bridge_word

phase_0.boundary_condition: Input: public key IMASM word with 6 primitives at promoted values. Output: private key IMASM word with all primitives at original base values. Precondition: well-formed public key word. Postcondition: private key recovered via B-state dialetheic fixed point.

TANCH.justification: Terminal anchor confirming retrieval is complete

AFWD.justification: Each AFWD advances one primitive in the promotion chain

AREV.justification: Each AREV unwinds one primitive back toward its private-key value

CLINK.justification: Links current primitive with next in the promotion chain

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: self-referential closure or data primitive push
IMSCRIB.justification: Primitive glyphs act as data pushes encoded as self-reference; also marks closure points where retrieval becomes identity

FSPLIT.chosen_element: key pair split into public point and private scalar
FSPLIT.justification: The secp256k1 key pair naturally bifurcates into public and private components

FFUSE.chosen_element: bridge word recovers private key from public key
FFUSE.justification: The 87-glyph promotion cycle re-fuses the public key word back into the private key word

EVALT.justification: Affirmative branch holding promoted primitive values

EVALF.justification: Negative branch holding base primitive values

ENGAGR.chosen_element: dialetheic B-state — T and F simultaneously
ENGAGR.justification: Bottleneck where public and private primitive values coexist; 6 TF landings at positions 29-34

IFIX.chosen_element: permanent record of the recovered key
IFIX.justification: Private key once recovered is fixed and cannot be reversed

phase_2.split_element: FSPLIT splits key pair into public point P and private scalar n
phase_2.fuse_element: FFUSE applies bridge word to public key word to recover private key

phase_3.true_description: 01 — T-state — public key primitives at promoted values
phase_3.false_description: 10 — F-state — private key primitives at base values
phase_3.both_description: 11 — B-state — dialetheic hold where T and F coexist at the ENGAGR bottleneck

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Belnap FOUR VM translates mixed opcode and data glyphs into register operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Sequential crystal-linking — each CLINK composes preceding primitive with next
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Belnap register holds 00 01 10 11 — ENGAGR at position 29 sets register to 11
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Strict sequential order — 82 T landings structural flow — 6 TF landings at dialetheic hold

phase_6.cycle_cost: One register transition per glyph — 68 inert weight steps cost zero — only dialetheic hold carries cost
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Register at void 00 — public key loaded — private key latent in the B-state
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Register at B 11 — private key fully recovered — bridge word has become retrieval identity
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: Delta S approximately zero — forward and reverse steps balance — ENGAGR hold is lattice meet not state transition

banked_count_check.verdict: 2 unit(s) of weight cleared with nothing banked behind them: the count was in the open when the reversal came
banked_count_check.remedy: open the region that holds the result BEFORE the region that computes it, and close them in that order, so the inner fuse folds into the enclosing frame rather than into the register

rotat_audit.verdict: PHASE-BEARING — moves under ROTAT: closed_walk, final_register
